questions.title: Why does the 'pingpong' warp‑specialization in FlashAttention‑3 require barrier synchronization and how does it improve FP16 throughput?
questions.question_body: In section 3.1 the authors describe a pingpong scheduling scheme that overlaps softmax on one warpgroup with GEMM on another. I understand that this is intended to hide the low‑throughput exp calls behind the WGMMA matmul, but I’m confused about how the `bar.sync` barriers actually enforce this overlap, and why two separate warpgroups are needed. Also, what would happen if we omitted the barriers or used only one warpgroup? Does this change the theoretical FLOP utilization?

questions.title: How does FP8 WGMMA’s k‑major constraint affect memory layout for value tensors in FlashAttention‑3?
questions.question_body: Section 3.3 states that FP8 WGMMA only accepts k‑major operands and that a value tile must be contiguous in the sequence length dimension. Since typical value tensors are stored contiguous along the head dimension, how does FlashAttention‑3 achieve the required layout without expensive preprocessing? Can you walk through the in‑kernel transpose using LDSM/STSM and explain why it works for FP8 but not for FP16?
